hlni.insight: One unlabeled course activity cannot prove which degree it belongs to.
hlni.audienceGap: Students often assume specific subjects belong exclusively to B.Com or BBA based on anecdotal stereotypes.
hlni.viewerChange: Encourages students to stop guessing and start asking for official evidence when comparing programmes.
hlni.support: Logical reasoning: missing contextual links make exclusive classification impossible.
hlni.payoff: The viewer learns to replace guessing with a critical question: 'What specific document links this to the degree?'

creativeAngle: A visual puzzle challenging the assumption that a single course module defines a degree.
objective: To teach students how to critically evaluate degree comparisons by identifying missing evidence.
targetAudience: A broad +2 student audience discovering ideas, courses, or student experiences

shots.name: The Challenge Screen
shots.visual: A split-screen digital card flip showing 'Case Study: Managing a supply chain crisis.'

shots.name: The Reveal
shots.visual: Card flips to reveal a stamp saying 'Not enough info.'
shots.dialogue: Answer: Not enough info. You can't categorize a degree from one isolated activity.

shots.name: The Practical Inquiry
shots.visual: Text appears over a blurred university document graphic.
shots.dialogue: What specific document links this activity to a BBA degree? Always check the source.
shots.onscreenText: What specific document links this activity to a BBA degree?
shots.cameraPerformance: Clean graphic overlay, slow fade out.

productionNotes.editing: Snappy, rhythmic cuts synced to the card flip.
productionNotes.sound: Subtle 'pop' sound effect on card flip.
props: Digital tablet or high-resolution screen overlay
productionNotes.casting: One student creator, relatable and natural.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Use a misleading example to demonstrate that one module cannot define a degree, teaching students to demand verifiable evidence.

selected.title: The Missing Link Challenge
selected.audienceGap: Students believe they can identify a degree just by looking at a single course module.
selected.hlni: One unlabeled example does not prove which category or programme contains it. An exclusive claim needs information that actually links the example to that category.
selected.viewerChange: Teaches that one example cannot prove degree categorization without linked evidence.
selected.concept: A visual puzzle presents an activity and asks if it is B.Com or BBA, revealing the lack of sufficient info.
selected.device: An interactive digital card flip that challenges the viewer's assumption.
selected.support: This is a reasoning limit: absent information cannot establish an exclusive classification.
methodSteps: Present one example without a source linking it to a category.
Separate a plausible guess from what the available information proves.
Identify the exact missing source or information needed to decide.
selected.interpretationRule: Answer not enough information when the necessary link is absent, then name the evidence that would resolve it.
selected.visibleProof: A forced-choice guess is replaced by a justified third answer and a precise request for missing evidence.
selected.payoff: Answer not enough information when the necessary link is absent, then name the evidence that would resolve it.
selected.limitations: Do not assert that the example belongs to both degrees, or to either one, without actual curriculum evidence.

demonstration.observation: The viewer cannot link the activity to a specific degree with current facts.

comparedWith.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
comparedWith.device: A split-screen view shows a student filling out a worksheet while an overlay highlights the three critical questions.

comparedWith.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
comparedWith.device: A casual conversation where they record one struggle on a post-it note.

comparedWith.hlni: One unlabeled example does not prove which category or programme contains it. An exclusive claim needs information that actually links the example to that category.
comparedWith.device: An interactive digital card flip that challenges the viewer's assumption.

conceptSelection.contrast: Trust uses a structural audit to build credibility; Connection uses a relatable peer-interaction to lower anxiety; Discovery uses a logical puzzle to challenge the assumption that degrees can be identified by single, isolated examples.
